result:
: each sector's weight and risk equal the direct holdings plus ETF weight and risk times the sector share, rounded to 4 dp (§5).
- `test_engine_lookthrough_removes_broad_market_when_all_etfs_are_covered`: no `Broad market` bucket remains, while `Bonds` and `Gold` do (§5, §7.3).
- `test_engine_lookthrough_keeps_weight_and_risk_totals_and_sort_order`: weights and risks still sum to 1 and groups stay sorted by descending risk (§5).
- `test_engine_lookthrough_changes_only_the_sector_group_and_the_flag`: everything except `groups.sector`, `lookthrough` and `assumptions` equals the no-file run (§5, CLAUDE.md). `assumptions` is excluded because it may gain a look-through line.
- `test_engine_lookthrough_is_deterministic`: two runs with the same seed give identical output (§5).
- `test_engine_lookthrough_leaves_an_uncovered_etf_as_broad_market`: an uncovered ETF (ESGV) stays in `Broad market` while SPY and XIU.TO are split (§3.2, §5).
- `test_engine_lookthrough_ignores_rows_of_etfs_not_held`: rows for an ETF not in the portfolio change nothing (§5).
- `test_h6_adds_the_etf_lookthrough_part_and_flags_a_violation_the_direct_part_hides`: H6 is 0.05 direct plus 0.15 through ETFs, so 0.20 against a 0.15 limit is a violation with no `unknown` (§7.3).
- `test_h6_passes_with_the_same_total_under_a_higher_limit_and_no_unknown`: the same total under a 0.25 limit passes with value 0.20 and no `unknown` (§7.3).
- `test_h6_other_employer_sector_uses_that_sectors_shares`: for Health Care the value is JNJ 0.05 plus SPY 0.30 × 0.20, so 0.11, and the status follows the limit (§7.3).
- `test_h6_bond_and_gold_etfs_do_not_count_for_the_employer_sector`: only equity ETFs are looked through; bond and gold ETFs add nothing and raise no `unknown` (§7.3).
- `test_h6_uncovered_etf_still_emits_unknown_for_its_part_only`: the covered part is counted and one `unknown` of 0.10 is emitted for ESGV (§7.3). The unknown's value uses the stricter reading (see `SPEC-AMBIGUITY` in the test).
- `test_h6_without_lookthrough_rows_is_the_p0_behaviour` (2 params): with no file or a header-only file, H6 reports the direct 0.05 plus one `unknown` for the 0.50 of ETF weight (§7.3).
- `test_h6_checks_keep_the_section_7_3_shape_and_are_hard`: each H6 result has the documented keys, `kind` hard, `confidence` 1.0, and derives from `max_employer_sector_weight` (§7.3).
- `test_h10_with_lookthrough_uses_the_max_sector_share_and_emits_no_unknown` (2 params): H10 compares the top sector's risk (IT 0.45) with the limit and emits no `unknown` (§7.3).
- `test_h10_without_lookthrough_excludes_broad_market_and_flags_it_unknown`: with look-through off, `Broad market` is out of the max and reported `unknown` (§7.3).
- `test_h10_end_to_end_with_lookthrough_has_no_unknown_and_tops_the_real_sector_split`: real look-through output feeds H10, the subject is the riskiest sector, and the status flips at the limit (§5, §7.3).
- `test_h10_without_a_file_end_to_end_keeps_the_unknown`: with no file, the `Broad market` `unknown` stays (§7.3).
- `test_h11_sector_weights_alone_never_pass_or_violate_an_etf`: sector weights don't clear an ETF, so it stays `unknown` (§7.3, §19). The spec says look-through removes "most unknowns" on H11, so this is the stricter reading (see `SPEC-AMBIGUITY` in the test).
- `test_h11_lookthrough_file_does_not_change_a_held_stocks_h11_result`: a held stock with no tag row is `unknown` with or without the sector file (§7.3).
- `test_h11_still_violates_on_a_sourced_tag_row_with_lookthrough_on`: a human-sourced tag row still gives a violation, and ETFs stay `unknown` (§3.2, §7.3).
- `test_metrics_with_lookthrough_carry_a_boolean_flag_and_stay_report_schema_valid`: the metrics have `lookthrough` True and still validate against the report `metrics` definition (§13).
- `test_sources_md_and_readme_document_the_file_and_the_four_etfs`: SOURCES.md and README name `etf_sector_weights`, look-through, XIU.TO, SPY, QQQ and ESGV, and SOURCES.md names `source_url` and `as_of` (task P2.13, §19).
